paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: This figure illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a threshold of 1e-2 across different layers of a model, comparing three conditions. The X-axis is labeled "Layer" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The Y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are plotted. The first line, shown in blue with a dashed style, represents "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03"; it starts near 0.18 at layer 0, drops quickly to around 0.04 by layer 3, and remains relatively stable between 0.02 and 0.05 throughout the remaining layers, ending near 0.0 at layer 23. The second line, shown in orange with a dotted style, represents "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44"; it begins at 1.0 at layer 0, decreases in a generally downward trend through the layers, passing through approximately 0.7 at layer 5, 0.47 at layer 9, and continuing to decline with some fluctuation to around 0.15–0.20 in the range of layers 15–18, before rising slightly and fluctuating between 0.1 and 0.4 in the final layers. The third line, shown in green with a dash-dot style, represents "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33"; it starts near 0.95 at layer 0, decreases steeply to about 0.4 by layer 7, continues declining to approximately 0.2 around layer 10, then fluctuates between roughly 0.05 and 0.2 from layers 12 to 20, with a notable rise to approximately 0.4 at layer 23. The title of the figure reads "Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2."
model_annotations.Chinese: This figure shows the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output values below a threshold of 1e-2 across different layers of a model. The x-axis represents Layer, on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents Sparsity Ratio, on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are plotted. The first line, labeled "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03," is a blue dashed line that starts near 0.18 at layer 0, quickly drops to around 0.04 by layer 3, and remains relatively stable near 0.02–0.04 throughout the remaining layers, ending near 0.00 at layer 23. The second line, labeled "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44," is an orange dotted line that starts at approximately 1.0 at layer 0, decreases in a generally declining trend through the layers, reaching around 0.47 at layer 9, continuing to drop to approximately 0.17 around layer 15, and then fluctuating between roughly 0.08 and 0.40 in the later layers, ending near 0.10 at layer 23. The third line, labeled "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33," is a green dash-dot line that starts at approximately 0.95 at layer 0, decreases steeply to around 0.50 by layer 6, continues declining to approximately 0.20 near layer 11, then fluctuates at lower values between roughly 0.08 and 0.15 from layers 13 to 20, before showing a slight increase to approximately 0.10 at layer 23.
model_annotations.English: This plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output values below a threshold of 1e-2 across different layers of a model, comparing three conditions: before gating, after gating, and after an average gate. The x-axis is labeled "Layer" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The first line, shown in blue with a dashed style, represents the sparsity ratio before gating with an average of 0.03; it starts at approximately 0.18 at layer 0, decreases to around 0.04 by layer 5, remains relatively stable near 0.03–0.04 through layers 5 to 20, and drops to approximately 0.0 by layer 23. The second line, shown in orange with a dotted style, represents the sparsity ratio after gating with an average of 0.44; it starts at 1.0 at layer 0, declines steeply to about 0.48 by layer 8, continues decreasing to approximately 0.17 around layer 15, then fluctuates between roughly 0.08 and 0.40 from layer 16 to layer 23. The third line, shown in green with a dash-dot style, represents the sparsity ratio after an average gate with an average of 0.33; it starts at approximately 0.95 at layer 0, decreases to about 0.60 by layer 5, continues declining to around 0.22 by layer 10, then fluctuates at lower values between approximately 0.05 and 0.15 from layer 12 to layer 23.
model_annotations.German: This figure displays the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across transformer layers, using a threshold of 1e-2. The x-axis is labeled "Layer" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to approximately 23, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Three lines are shown. The first line, labeled "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03," is a blue dashed line that starts at approximately 0.18 at layer 0, quickly drops to around 0.04 by layer 3, remains relatively stable between 0.02 and 0.05 across subsequent layers, and decreases to approximately 0.01 by layer 23. The second line, labeled "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44," is an orange dotted line that starts at approximately 1.0 at layer 0, generally decreases across layers with values around 0.90 at layer 2, 0.70 at layer 5, 0.47 at layer 9, drops to around 0.28 at layer 12, continues to decrease to around 0.17 at layer 15, and fluctuates between approximately 0.10 and 0.40 in the final layers, ending near 0.35 at layer 23. The third line, labeled "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33," is a green dash-dot line that starts at approximately 0.95 at layer 0, decreases steeply through the early layers to about 0.60 at layer 5, continues declining to approximately 0.20 at layer 10, then fluctuates at lower values between roughly 0.05 and 0.22 from layers 12 to 23, ending at approximately 0.10 at layer 23.
